analyzed_vuln.description: xmlParseEntityDecl assumes six bytes are available after seeing '<!ENTITY' via CMP6(CUR_PTR,...), then unconditionally executes SKIP(6). In this PoV, malformed/short DTD entity declaration data in the internal subset lets CUR_PTR be at/near the end of the current input buffer (including entity-expanded boundaries), so SKIP/NEXT reads past the valid buffer and triggers a 1-byte global out-of-bounds read. Root cause is missing post-match input-boundary validation before advancing parser cursor in entity-declaration parsing.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Triggered through the schema fuzz harness (xmlSchemaParse -> xmlSchemaAddSchemaDoc -> XML parser) with an XML containing a DOCTYPE internal subset and malformed <!ENTITY declaration bytes. The input must drive xmlParseInternalSubset/xmlParseMarkupDecl into xmlParseEntityDecl with insufficient remaining bytes around the ENTITY keyword (or across parser input boundary), so SKIP(6) dereferences beyond valid input. No special runtime options are required beyond normal schema parsing of attacker-controlled document content.
